quest.title: Shadow of Yore
quest.description: You and Paimon recognize a familiar face as you come aboard the Pearl Galley...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Mora x19675, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh? I didn't think I would see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #Yes, we had the fortune of meeting {NICKNAME} not too long ago. They are quite a knowledgeable and talented pair, and a pleasure to be around.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, we were just discussing the history of Rex Lapis. Would you like to listen?

dialogues.speaker: Hanxue
dialogues.text: This good sir seems not to appreciate the almighty power of the Lord of Geo. As a professional archaeologist, I am inclined to correct some of his erroneous views.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: We are discussing the whereabouts of the first Mora.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The first Mora?

response.speaker: Yixuan
response.text: As everyone knows, the Lord of Geo taught the ancient people of Liyue the craft of smelting, creating goods that allowed them to develop trade with the early nations of that time.

response.speaker: Yixuan
response.text: Today, Liyue holds the sole right to cast Mora in the entire continent of Teyvat. The world's very first Mora should have been cast by the hands of the Lord of Geo himself thousands of years ago.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: According to my research — as well as my own hypothesis — I believe that this coin of unique historical significance has been passed down secretly through the years as a kind of token.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: For example, perhaps the Qixing who control Liyue use it in some kind of unknown ceremony they hold when they come to power...

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: No, no, no... My research indicates that the first Mora coin is not such a simple thing.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Mora is a catalyst — this we all know. Even today, Mora is used in the mystic arts for its curious properties of weapon enhancement.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: The world's first Mora would no doubt possess the strongest power. My next historical treatise will boldly expound on the newest findings from my intense, decade-long research!

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: That is, that the Lord of Geo used this original Mora as a catalyst to enhance a dagger and a sword.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "A dagger and a sword"?

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Well, buy the book when it comes out to read the full story. For now, I will only reveal this: the one who finds the dagger shall become supreme in Liyue, and the one who finds the sword may be crowned Liyue's sovereign—

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I... can't say I agree.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Let us not speak of the authenticity of the dagger and sword first... But Mora and money came about simply because they are a convenient measure of a contract's value.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Rex Lapis just meant for Mora to serve as a "catalyst" for people to exchange and trade.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The world's first Mora is probably just an ordinary coin created by Rex Lapis. As for its fate? The same as all Mora, I suspect — it was simply spent somewhere.

response.speaker: Yixuan
response.text: Hmm... I think that Mr. Hanxue's hypothesis seems reasonable. Mr. Zhongli's argument, on the other hand, lacks any evidence. How can you so easily dismiss the Lord of Geo's profound foresight?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No — no, I am not debating right or wrong. I am simply stating a fact.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Enough! Do you think you understand the Lord of Geo more than me?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I know but little about history and I wouldn't dare to brag. But discussion is meaningless if everyone has the same opinion, no?

response.speaker: Yixuan
response.text: Well then, answer me this: Long ago, when Liyue Harbor was being constructed, the Lord of Geo taught the people how to build houses. The model home he used to teach them was completely cast from Mora, correct?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That is correct, indeed.

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Okay then, tell me: Why would the Lord of Geo do something so extravagant if not because of the mystical power that Mora contains?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There's a simple explanation, really. To the God of Wealth and Commerce, what material is easier to get than Mora?

response.speaker: Hanxue
response.text: Oh... Huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's like you're telling someone else's tale.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hehe, I mean... I am talking about Rex Lapis.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Excuse me, sir! Uh... I have some questions about archaeology. Can we find somewhere quiet to chat? I mean, if it's okay with you.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh, it's no problem at all. But may my friend accompany us? Perhaps they could be of some help.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Of course. They can come if that's what pleases you, sir. Let's go.

choices.text: I'm just here for a good story.
No one knows better than him...
No one knows better than him...

talks.objective: Head to the stern and ask Wanyan about her problem

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: What I'm about to say is a bit disrespectful of the Lord of Geo and would draw a lot of angry looks... so it's best to discuss this somewhere quiet.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Your argument just now exhibited acuteness of speech and thought. Most importantly, you don't fall for the boasting and acting of the others. You remain objective.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: So I have a question for you, perhaps you will answer differently from other scholars... Do you think that all the gods that the Geo Archon killed were evil?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...Let's not analyze it in terms of good versus evil. Rex Lapis placed great importance on the integrity of contracts, so any gods he killed certainly must have broken some kind of contract.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, the Lord of Geo wouldn't kill the innocent.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: But when I was doing some research, I learned about the legend of the God of Salt.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: The God of Salt, Havria, was a very kind god, but she encountered Morax one day in battle...

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Morax used a rather underhanded trick to... assassinate her.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This... this bit of history is a long story. But you may not like the truth when you hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Don't worry, please tell me what you know! This event... I have already searched for answers for a long time.

choices.text: You look a bit embarrassed, Zhongli.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No, it's just... Where should I begin?

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Over here! Mr. Zhongli, I've been looking for you! Ah, so you're over here all this time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Put down your weapon and stay back! Otherwise... Ah... Paimon's reporting you to the Millelith!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: First of all, I'm not holding a weapon!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Ugh... There's no need to overreact, now. I'm simply an archaeological researcher from Snezhnaya, I'm not here for trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Fatui say that every time.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: But this time, I registered with the Liyue Ministry of Civil Affairs. I could show you the official documentation if you want to see it.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: I will be conducting an archaeological survey here, the results of which will all be shared with the Ministry.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: I heard that Wangsheng Funeral Parlor had a consultant named Zhongli with immense knowledge of ancient history and archaeology. So I paid Wangsheng Funeral Parlor a handsome amount to hire Zhongli as my own consultant while I'm in town.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So you mean to say that this is work for the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, yes?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Well since it's work, I don't have a choice. A consultant of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor must respect their duty.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Of course you would be such a reasonable man! Well then, let's head out now, shall we?

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Wait, if you are studying archaeology, can I go too? I am also a scholar in this field, so I can help.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #That will give us a chance to continue the topic we were just discussing. Oh, and you should tag along too, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: This experience may be of help to you on your future adventures.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It is a story from before the rise of The Seven... Although the God of Salt has already perished, it will still be a meaningful experience for your journey.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: This is— Wait, this is an archaeological expedition, not a tour group! That's too many people.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But this friend of mine has a treasure-finding talent surpassed by no one. It will surely be of great help to us.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Oh? What talent?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: If my friend espies a treasure chest, they will absolutely find a way to open it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon's good at that, too!

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Well... That is quite enticing. Alright then.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Well, let's go. There's no time to waste. When the Overlord of the Vortex was crushed by the Jade Chamber recently, perhaps something of interest was washed ashore...

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: An ancient artifact would be good, traces of ancient activity would be great, but a piece of the god's limb would be even better... Who knows what surprises we may find...?

choices.text: I don't really know anything about archaeology.
I think it's best to be cautious.
What do you want!? Spit it out!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Quite so. I don't know where to begin.
